problem:
Find the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}$ given that $3a-5x=b$ and

$$
a=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 5 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-13 \\ 5 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$
worked_solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3a-5x & =b \\ -5x & =b-3a \\ x & =-\frac{1}{5}(b-3a) \\ x & =-\frac{1}{5}([\begin{aligned}-13 \\ 5 \\ -3\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]) \\ x & =-\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ -15\end{aligned}] \\ x & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-1+2=1.$
